name: Humphry Davy
summary: British chemist who isolated alkali and alkaline earth metals using electrolysis.

name: Royal Institution
summary: London-based organization dedicated to scientific education and research.

name: Penzance
summary: Town in Cornwall, England, birthplace of Humphry Davy.

name: Cornwall
summary: County in southwestern England known for tin mining.

name: Michael Faraday
summary: English scientist who succeeded Davy at the Royal Institution and developed electromagnetism.

name: Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac
summary: French chemist known for gas laws and rivalry with Davy over iodine.

name: Alessandro Volta
summary: Italian physicist who invented the voltaic pile battery.

name: Jöns Jacob Berzelius
summary: Swedish chemist who refined atomic masses and chemical symbols.

name: Davy safety lamp
summary: Miner's lamp designed by Davy with wire gauze to prevent ignition of firedamp.

name: voltaic pile
summary: First electric battery invented by Volta, used by Davy for electrolysis.

name: Napoleon
summary: French emperor who awarded Davy a prize for electrochemical work.

name: Count Rumford
summary: American-born British scientist who founded the Royal Institution.

name: École Polytechnique
summary: French engineering school where Gay-Lussac and Thénard worked.

name: University of North Texas
summary: University where the authors James L. and Virginia R. Marshall are affiliated.

name: Camborne School of Mines
summary: Mining school in Cornwall associated with the University of Exeter.

name: University of Exeter
summary: University associated with the Camborne School of Mines.
